questions.text: A student reviews the following situation: a rapidly dividing intestinal cell. Why do smaller cells generally exchange materials with the environment more efficiently than larger cells?

questions.explain: A higher surface area-to-volume ratio supports faster exchange relative to internal demand.

Correct. More membrane area relative to volume allows faster exchange per unit volume.

questions.text: A student reviews the following situation: a rapidly dividing intestinal cell. Which statement correctly compares facilitated diffusion and active transport?
choices: Facilitated diffusion moves substances down their gradient without ATP, whereas active transport moves substances against a gradient using energy
Both processes always move substances against their gradients
Facilitated diffusion can occur only for water
Only active transport uses membrane proteins
questions.explain: The energy requirement and direction relative to the gradient distinguish these transport modes.
choice_explanations: Correct. This distinction matches the definitions of the two transport processes.
Incorrect. Facilitated diffusion moves down a gradient.
Incorrect. Many ions and polar molecules also use facilitated diffusion.
Incorrect. Facilitated diffusion also depends on membrane proteins.

Facilitated diffusion can occur only for water
Facilitated diffusion moves substances down their gradient without ATP, whereas active transport moves substances against a gradient using energy
Only active transport uses membrane proteins
questions.explain: The energy requirement and direction relative to the gradient distinguish these transport modes.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. Facilitated diffusion moves down a gradient.
Incorrect. Many ions and polar molecules also use facilitated diffusion.
Correct. This distinction matches the definitions of the two transport processes.
Incorrect. Facilitated diffusion also depends on membrane proteins.
questions.image_alt: Phospholipid bilayer diagram showing simple diffusion, facilitated diffusion through a channel, and active transport against a gradient using ATP.

questions.text: A student reviews the following situation: a rapidly dividing intestinal cell. A red blood cell placed in a highly concentrated salt solution shrivels. Which term best describes the outside solution?
choices: hydrophobic
hypertonic
hypotonic
isotonic
questions.explain: Water leaves a cell in a hypertonic environment, causing it to shrink.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. Hydrophobic describes nonpolar substances, not relative solute concentration.
Correct. A hypertonic solution draws water out of the cell, causing shrinkage.
Incorrect. A hypotonic solution would cause net water entry instead.
Incorrect. An isotonic solution would produce little or no net water movement.

questions.explain: Compartmentalization allows different biochemical conditions to exist in the same cell.

Incorrect. Enzymes are still required inside compartments.

questions.text: A student reviews the following situation: a rapidly dividing intestinal cell. Why do phospholipids spontaneously arrange into bilayers in water?

Correct. The amphipathic nature of phospholipids drives bilayer formation.
Incorrect. Ribosomes do not assemble membranes this way.

questions.text: A student analyzes this experiment: diffusion through agar cubes of different sizes. A membrane protein inhibitor sharply reduces glucose uptake only when glucose would normally move down its gradient. Which process is most likely blocked?
choices: bulk transport
facilitated diffusion
osmosis
DNA replication
questions.explain: A drop in protein-mediated passive transport is characteristic of blocked facilitated diffusion.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. The description focuses on protein-mediated transport of a small solute, not vesicles.
Correct. Glucose often requires a transport protein to move passively down its gradient.
Incorrect. Osmosis concerns water, not glucose.
Incorrect. Replication is unrelated to membrane glucose uptake.

questions.text: A student analyzes this experiment: diffusion through agar cubes of different sizes. A table shows that diffusion time to the center rises steeply as cell diameter increases. Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: Large cells always have higher surface area-to-volume ratios
Diffusion rate is unrelated to distance inside cells
Increasing cell size can make internal transport less efficient
Only eukaryotic cells are limited by diffusion
questions.explain: Diffusion limitations are one reason cells benefit from small size or internal transport systems.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. The ratio actually decreases with increasing size.
Incorrect. The table shows the opposite.
Correct. Longer diffusion distances are a major reason cells remain relatively small.
Incorrect. Both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells face distance constraints.

questions.text: A student analyzes this experiment: diffusion through agar cubes of different sizes. A student adds a molecule to both sides of a membrane and later finds it accumulated on one side only when ATP is available. Which process is most consistent with the result?
choices: active transport
osmosis
simple diffusion
facilitated diffusion
questions.explain: Energy dependence and gradient buildup point to active transport.
choice_explanations: Correct. Accumulation against a gradient with ATP dependence indicates active transport.
Incorrect. Osmosis refers specifically to water movement.
Incorrect. Simple diffusion does not require ATP and cannot build concentration gradients.
Incorrect. Facilitated diffusion is passive and does not require ATP.
